notes: Identity independently checked: repository cover identifies the post-review version of Third-World Copycats to Emerging Multinationals: Institutional Changes and Organizational Transformation in the Indian Pharmaceutical Industry, Raveendra Chittoor, M.B. Sarkar, Sougata Ray, and Preet S. Aulakh, February 2009, Organization Science 20(1), 187–205, DOI 10.1287/orsc.1080.0377. Title page and manuscript authors agree. This is primary author-manuscript text, with methods, results, references, Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–3 through manuscript p. 44, rather than an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed. Assigned original study, description, original effect-size type and locators are all null/empty. Reference identifies a paper but does not identify an outcome, hypothesis, coefficient, model or subgroup. No target assigned by row order or numeric matching. Candidate sample roles only: p. 18 gives 206 domestic firms in an unbalanced panel and 1,104 observations (firm-years); Table 2, p. 40 gives 1104 observations in each of Models 1–6; Table 3, p. 41 gives ROS Model 1 = 1103 observations and ROA Model 2 = 1104 observations. P. 18 excludes 35 foreign subsidiaries, 22 firms founded after 1995, and 76 additional firms under minimum-sales/data-availability criteria; missing firm-years and one-year predictor lags are documented. The particular missing observation in the ROS model is not explained in Table 3. P. 27 additionally describes 31 firms over three years for supplementary innovation-capability analyses; no target-specific analytic observation count is established for those tests. None of these candidate sample counts is promoted to the assigned N; no arithmetic derivation performed. Candidate tests: Table 2 Model 1/main-effects narrative p. 23 reports international technology resources b = 0.25, p < .001; international financial resources b = .11, p < .05; business-group affiliation b = -0.10, p < .001. Table 2 Model 6 reports technology-by-time b = 0.08, p < .10; finance-by-time b = 0.01, p > .10 (narrative p. 24); technology-by-business-group b = -0.12, p < .05; finance-by-business-group b = -0.01, p < .10. Table 2 explicitly identifies unstandardized regression coefficients, with robust standard errors and one-tailed significance. Table 3 explicitly identifies unstandardized regression coefficients: product-market internationalization predicts ROS b = 51.55, p < .001 and ROA b = 27.61, p < .10; its square term predicts ROS b = -5.58, p < .001 and ROA b = -2.63, p < .10. Table 3 tests are one-tailed. Figures 2–3/p. 24–25 also contain time-period and business-group subgroup coefficients, and p. 27 reports additional correlations and an R&D-intensity regression. Multiple coefficients and model tests are present, with no supplied locator selecting one. No conversion or standardization attempted. Only n_o and es_value_o assigned; all other fields are unassigned placeholders.
